newsitem.title: UK: Homosexuals tortured, killed around world - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Homosexuals tortured, killed around world - Amnesty.

text.p: Homosexuals around the world are being killed, tortured and imprisoned, Amnesty International said in a report on gay human rights on Wednesday.
"In countries all over the world, men and women are harassed, abducted, imprisoned, tortured and even murdered for their sexual identity," Amnesty said in a report called "Breaking the Silence."

The international pressure group, whose British division put together the report, said gay men and lesbians were particularly vulnerable to human rights abuses and faced prosecution in up to 60 countries for their sexual preferences.
"Amnesty International shines a light into some very dark corners," the report's author, Dan Jones, told reporters.
The report said Colombian death squads target and kill hundreds of gay men and transvestites and call it social cleansing.
In Iran, homosexuality is punishable by the death penalty. "Those found guilty may suffer execution by public stoning," the report said.
The human rights pressure group sought to highlight the plight of persecuted gays by singling out individual cases.
The decapitated body of a Brazilian councillor was found on a rubbish dump after he was denounced for his bisexuality.
"For gays in Colombia, there is no rule of law. The only programme the government has for people like me is a programme to kill us," said Colombian male prostitute Luis Alberto.
A gay Turk named only as Ali said after fleeing his country: "Because I am homosexual, I have been sexually abused and raped many times and in unimaginable ways while being held at police stations."
The report praised South Africa for becoming the first nation to include sexual orientation in the anti-discrimination provisions of its constitution.
Ten U.S. states were lauded for prohibiting discriminatiion on the grounds of sexual orientation.
But Amnesty called for the decriminalisation of homosexuality around the world, citing such countries as Nigeria, Romania and India where it is still illegal.
"The language of these laws varies but the common effect is to stigmatise lesbians and gay men as criminals," Amnesty said.
It said that now that AIDS is often perceived as a gay plague, AIDS prevention activists were suffering from human rights abuses.
